spec.description: Subscribe to Open/High/Low/Close (OHLC) candle data at a given interval for one or more currency pairs. Updates are generated on trade events.

symbol.description: Currency pairs to subscribe to, e.g. `["BTC/USD", "MATIC/GBP"]`.

channel.description: The channel this push belongs to.

type.description: Whether this push is the initial snapshot or an incremental update.

timestamp.description: RFC3339 timestamp of this push. Not documented in the channel's field reference, but present on every worked example on the doc page.

items.title: OhlcCandle
items.description: One symbol's OHLC candle for the subscribed interval.

symbol.description: The symbol of the currency pair, e.g. `"BTC/USD"`.

open.description: The opening trade price within the interval.

high.description: The highest trade price within the interval.

low.description: The lowest trade price within the interval.

close.description: The last trade price within the interval.

vwap.description: Volume weighted average trade price within the interval.

trades.description: Number of trades within the interval.

volume.description: Total traded volume, in base currency terms, within the interval.

interval_begin.description: RFC3339 timestamp of the start of the interval.

interval.description: The timeframe of this candle's interval, in minutes.

timestamp.description: RFC3339 timestamp of the start of the interval. Deprecated -- use `interval_begin`.

notes: The message frame's top-level `timestamp` (distinct from each candle's own deprecated `data[].timestamp`) is not in the page's `ResponseField` list for the Snapshot/Update section, but appears in both of its worked JSON examples, so it is kept as a documented-by-example field rather than dropped. `data[].timestamp` is kept despite being marked deprecated, per rule 7 (drop no documented field); `interval_begin` is its documented replacement. `interval` has no documented `default` (unlike `depth`/`snapshot` on sibling channels), so none is declared.
